decisions.reason: The approved Hero V was already required to remain unchanged as the fixed reference. The source confirms its restoration and expands the separate preservation policy without changing the Hero V geometry requirement.
The candidate already requires precise alignment of the É accent and Hero V highest points using the unchanged Hero V as the reference. The source restates that rule without changing it.

The candidate already requires literal duplication of the approved Hero V terminal geometry rather than an interpreted accent. The source reports a failure to preserve that rule but does not modify its required value.
The existing state already requires the second V to rise above E and L while remaining below the Hero V and É accent peak. The source restates this hierarchy without changing it.
The source addresses the second V's height hierarchy, not its construction method, terminal derivation, or right-arm reach. The candidate's construction and character state remains unchanged.

The source requires retention of the already established architectural E and L forms but introduces no new construction principle or terminal constraint. Preservation is represented by the source Requirement rather than duplicated here.
The design-preservation decision does not affect accepted review-image formats or file accessibility.
The source concerns preservation of wordmark geometry and architectural relationships and does not resume or alter the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
The source does not change the wordmark's kerning, spacing, or cohesive-reading goal.
The preservation decision does not alter the all-caps case treatment or its selection status.
The source does not change the final production-ready artwork handoff requirement or specify any new export deliverable.
